newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-COX A CLASSY LOSER IN WORLD SERIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-COX A CLASSY LOSER IN WORLD SERIES.

text.p: Bobby Cox hates to lose, but the classy Atlanta Braves manager paid his respects to the New York Yankees after they won their fourth straight game to clinch the World Series on Saturday.

"I'm not too happy. Nobody likes to lose," Cox said after the 3-2 defeat to the Yanks in Game 6. "I don't care if this was the little league World Series. You want to win it because you're a competitor.

"If we had to lose, I sure don't mind losing to (Yankee manager) Joe Torre. He's a class act and a great manager. We're a class act, too, and we'll lose with class. We don't blame the umpires, we don't blame bad hops.
"We don't blame anything. We simply got beat."

Cox vented his frustrations over the umpiring while on the field Saturday, and was ejected in the fifth inning for blasting third base umpire Tim Welke on his way back to the dugout after arguing a call at second base.

Welke had angered the Braves with his ball and strike calls while behind the plate in Game 3 and had gotten in the way of right fielder Jermaine Dye, who failed to make a key catch in foul territory in Game 4.
"I thought it was time to say something," Cox explained. "I wasn't surprised I was ejected. I should have been ejected. I just wanted him to know he blew some plays."
On Saturday's contested play, Braves centre fielder Marquis Grissom was thrown out trying to advance to second on a Jimmy Key pitch that bounced away from catcher Joe Girardi.
Grissom, whose unlikely error on a fly ball led to the only run in New York's Game 5 victory, said the Braves had only themselves to blame for their Series defeat.
"We had an opportunity to score some runs and we didn't," said Grissom. "Everything else is meaningless."
The Braves lost the last three games by 8-6 (in 10 innings, after leading 6-0), 1-0 and 3-2.

The Braves, the dominant major league team of the '90s, have reached four of the last five World Series, but have only one Series crown to show for it -- last year's six-game triumph over the Cleveland Indians.
"People can say what they want," Grissom said about critics' claims that the Braves are under-achievers. "Four times in the World Series in five years speaks for itself."
"We'd like to have a few more world championships but we'll settle for the National League championship this year," said Cox.
John Smoltz, who won 24 games during the regular season, was masterful in the Series yet lost one of his two starts despite not yielding an earned run.
He thought the Yanks might have felt additional urgency since they were appearing in their first Series in 15 years.
"They may have had extra motivation," he said. "We've been here before.
Smoltz called it a "classic Series."
"I just give all the credit to them," said Smoltz. "They just flat out took the Series. They were down. They were out.
"That team did not lose a road post-season game and that's incredible."
Cox said he was not surprised by the quality of pitching in the Series.
"They contained us very well and we contained them," Cox said. "But they got one more run then we did."
